question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z<-1.94).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-2.0\,$ | $\,0.0212\,$ | $\,0.0207\,$ | $\,0.0202\,$ |
| $\,-1.9\,$ | $\,0.0268\,$ | $\,0.0262\,$ | $\,0.0256\,$ |
| $\,-1.8\,$ | $\,0.0336\,$ | $\,0.0329\,$ | $\,0.0322\,$ |

$P(Z<-1.94)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
If $Z∼N(0,1),$ then by the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Also, since $Z$ is continuous, 

$$
P(Z<-1.94)=P(Z\le -1.94)=Φ(-1.94).
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/8e2fd49cb0a74c1741c8155d50be56e5c002d7a0ed21adb5b49d2cc26ebbb24d.png)

Now, we determine the value of $Φ(-1.94)$ from the table:

- We first select the row that corresponds to $-1.9$ and the column that corresponds to $0.04.$

- Then, we take the value that lies at the intersection:

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-2.0\,$ | $\,0.0212\,$ | $\,0.0207\,$ | $\,0.0202\,$ |
| $\,-1.9\,$ | $\,0.0268\,$ | $\,0.0262\,$ | $\,0.0256\,$ |
| $\,-1.8\,$ | $\,0.0336\,$ | $\,0.0329\,$ | $\,0.0322\,$ |

Therefore, according to the table, we have

$$
P(Z\le -1.94)=Φ(-1.94)=0.0262.
$$
